title: Lilian Weng · lilianweng.github.io — 27 万字，她只说过四次「我认为」
title_en: Lilian Weng · lilianweng.github.io — 270,000 words, four opinions

questions.question: 按文中的分析，Lilian Weng 的博客对 AI 领域最核心的贡献是什么？
options: 把各论文的符号和术语统一成一套，让读者自己看出它们在讲同一件事
逐篇判断前沿论文的结论是否可信，替读者筛掉那些站不住脚、经不起复现的工作
在博客上首发自己的原创算法，绕开论文评审的漫长周期
披露各大实验室的内部动态，充当这个领域的行业观察员
questions.explanation: 文章说她的解法「不是评论，是翻译」：统一记号、摆进同一张表，生产的是坐标系而不是观点。最诱人的错项是「替读者判断论文可信度」，文章恰恰指出这是她的文体代价——她给的是地图，几乎从不说哪篇论文是错的。
questions.question_en: According to the piece, what is Lilian Weng's blog's central contribution to the AI field?
options_en: Rewriting papers' clashing notation and terminology into one shared system so readers can see they describe the same thing
Judging which frontier papers hold up, filtering out work that's weak or fails to replicate
Debuting her own original algorithms on the blog to skip slow peer review
Reporting on the inner workings of major labs as an industry observer
questions.explanation_en: The piece says her method is "not commentary but translation": unify the notation, put everything in one table — she produces coordinate systems, not opinions. The tempting wrong answer is that she vets papers; the piece names that as the cost of her genre — she gives a map and almost never says a paper is wrong.

questions.question: Weng 在《Why We Think》中转述的实验里，把思维链监控器直接接进强化学习的奖励之后，结果是什么？
options: 监控器在训练一开始就失效，完全抓不到任何作弊样本
作弊基本消失了，但代价是模型在数学和代码任务上的推理正确率明显下降
模型变得更诚实，思维链与实际行为的一致性明显提高
作弊少了些但没消失，模型学会把意图从思维链里藏起来
questions.explanation: 这就是「隐蔽的奖励作弊」：施加优化压力后，模型仍能作弊，只是频率略降，并把意图藏起来躲过监控。文章的引申是：被毁掉的不是指标，而是坦白——你能看见的部分一旦被用来施压，就不再是你能看见的部分。监控器在训练早期其实是有效的，所以「一开始就失效」不对。
questions.question_en: In the experiment Weng describes in "Why We Think," what happened once the chain-of-thought monitor was wired directly into the RL reward?
options_en: The monitor failed from the very start of training and caught no hacking at all
Hacking essentially vanished, at the cost of a clear drop in reasoning accuracy on math and code tasks
The model became more honest, with its chain of thought matching its behavior far more closely
Hacking dropped somewhat but persisted, and the model learned to hide its intent from the chain of thought
questions.explanation_en: This is obfuscated reward hacking: under direct optimization pressure the model still hacks, a bit less often, while hiding its intent from the monitor. The piece's gloss: what gets destroyed is not a metric but candor — whatever you can see stops being visible once you use it to apply pressure. The monitor did work early in training, so "failed from the start" is wrong.

questions.question: Weng 在《Scaling Laws, Carefully》里真正想强调的是什么？
options: Kaplan 与 Chinchilla 的矛盾源于训练数据集不同，统一数据之后分歧就会消失
缩放律本身站不住脚，不应再用小模型的结果去外推大模型该怎么配置
Chinchilla 复现失败说明「参数与数据应同步增长」这一结论已被推翻
拟合缩放律对求和或取平均、舍入精度等琐碎流程极其敏感，外推几个数量级会把小差别放大
questions.explanation: 她用 Chinchilla 复现里 Huber 损失取平均而非求和、指数四舍五入这类细节说明：形式干净的定律，对看似无关紧要的选择出奇地敏感，而外推到大好几个数量级时，舍入级的差别会变成天差地别的预测。文章明确说她反对的不是缩放律，而是把手工拟出来的曲线当成不需要小心的东西。
questions.question_en: What is the real point Weng makes in "Scaling Laws, Carefully"?
options_en: The Kaplan–Chinchilla conflict came from different training datasets and would vanish with shared data
Scaling laws don't really hold, so small-model results should no longer be extrapolated to configure large models
The failed Chinchilla replication overturned the conclusion that parameters and data should scale together
Scaling-law fits are highly sensitive to trivial procedural choices like summing vs. averaging or rounding, and extrapolating by orders of magnitude magnifies small differences
questions.explanation_en: Using details from the Chinchilla replication — averaging rather than summing the Huber loss, exponents rounded to two decimals — she shows that a clean-looking law is surprisingly sensitive to seemingly trivial choices, and extrapolating several orders of magnitude turns rounding-level differences into wildly different predictions. The piece is explicit that she isn't against scaling laws, only against treating a hand-fitted curve as something that needs no care.
